answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with earned throughput quotas: every identity starts with a tiny limit on how many offers it may post, and the limit grows only when peers attest completed, useful work. The violet ledger records each attestation, while a velvet-smooth reputation score decays when the agent idles or misbehaves, so bought identities lose reach. Building a thousand fakes is like building a jetty from loose sand: each one must still earn its own quota through genuine service, so the attacker's cost rises linearly with every fake identity.
